What is a Music License in India and why do I need it? A Music License in India is a legal authorization required to play copyrighted music in public spaces, including restaurants, events, retail stores, and more. Without a valid music license, using music for commercial purposes can lead to legal action from copyright holders. How does the Music License registration process work? The Music license registration process involves applying to the appropriate licensing authority, such as the Indian Performing Right Society (IPRS) or Phonographic Performance Ltd. (PPL), depending on the type of music usage. You’ll need to submit business details, venue information, and pay the applicable fees to complete the Music license registration. Who needs a Music License in India? Any business or individual using music for commercial gain—such as event organizers, café owners, broadcasters, or DJs—needs a Music License in India. Whether you're hosting live performances or playing recorded music, you must comply with licensing laws. What are the penalties for not completing Music license registration? Failure to obtain proper Music license registration can result in legal action, financial penalties, and even a ban on future music use. It is crucial for any commercial establishment using music to ensure they are fully licensed to avoid infringement issues.

sections.heading: Section 7
paragraphs: Music license gives permission to businesses to play recorded music or live concert on their premises legally. Section 2 (p) of the Copyright act, 1957, defines musical work as a work consisting of music and includes any graphical notation of such work but does not comprise any words or any act intended to be spoken, sung, or performed with music. There are two kinds of bodies that issue music licenses in India, namely, PPL (Phonographic Performance Limited) and IPRS (The Indian Performing Right Societies). PPL (Phonographic Performance Limited) is responsible for approving licenses for businesses like pubs and cafes for pre-recorded music. IPRS (The Indian Performing Right Societies) approves license to hotels, theatres, events premises, pubs, malls, and banquets for conducting live concerts.

Playing music without having a music license can result in legal actions in India, which may attract penalties. Music licenses protect the rights of musicians and artists and provide legal protection to businesses and individuals as well.

Sync License: In this category, already created music is aligned with various visual content. A wide range of users, including television commercials, advertising firms, film production companies, and others, requires music licenses.

Mechanical License: The objective of this music license in India is to make artists' works accessible to the public through CDs, published music online, or any other distribution method. The artist who holds the copyrights to their creations gets compensated for signing a contract for the distribution or duplication of their original work. A mechanical music license in India is required even for making a minor change in original components such as remixing, adding one’s own lyrics, changing anything of the original composition, etc.
Master License: It is issued along with the sync license. The pre-recorded music may be used in any audio-visual project by the license holder, but re-recording the song is not permitted.

Public Performance License: It is the most popular type of music license in India granted for the broadcasting of a copyrighted work of an artist. This license is needed by the businesses that play music in their jukeboxes or at public events like concerts.

Print Rights License: It is the indication of the physical copy of the sheet music that an artist has produced. It is required when someone prints the sheet music compilation or any time the sheet music of a copyrighted work is reproduced.

Theatrical License: The theatrical licenses are a kind of written permit in the theatre industry. This music license in India is needed whenever a copyrighted work is performed live in front of the audience.
An artist can effortlessly use the platform to display their talent to the audience by obtaining a music license.
Adhering to the conditions of the music license will prevent the music from being reproduced.
Public performances at pubs and restaurants are conducted only by obtaining license to play songs; it will attract more audiences and enhance the restaurant's reputation.

1. What is a Music License in India and why do I need it?

A Music License in India is a legal authorization required to play copyrighted music in public spaces, including restaurants, events, retail stores, and more. Without a valid music license, using music for commercial purposes can lead to legal action from copyright holders.
How does the Music License registration process work?

The Music license registration process involves applying to the appropriate licensing authority, such as the Indian Performing Right Society (IPRS) or Phonographic Performance Ltd. (PPL), depending on the type of music usage. You’ll need to submit business details, venue information, and pay the applicable fees to complete the Music license registration.
Who needs a Music License in India?

Any business or individual using music for commercial gain—such as event organizers, café owners, broadcasters, or DJs—needs a Music License in India. Whether you're hosting live performances or playing recorded music, you must comply with licensing laws.
What are the penalties for not completing Music license registration?

Failure to obtain proper Music license registration can result in legal action, financial penalties, and even a ban on future music use. It is crucial for any commercial establishment using music to ensure they are fully licensed to avoid infringement issues.
